data.description:
## Context
Gerrit Verify run 31846417650 dynamically attributed the recurring macOS long pole: `socket.getfqdn` consumed 35.013s inside `ThreadingHTTPServer` construction for the loopback editor fixture; constructor and fixture setup were 35.014s/35.020s. TCP bind was below the 1s instrumentation threshold. The test contract needs a real loopback HTTP server but does not consume `server_name`, so reverse DNS changes no asserted behavior. This violates the operator requirement that individual tests remain negligible and that average Verify duration stay within 20–30 minutes without reducing coverage. pip explicitly bypasses the same ~30s HTTPServer reverse-DNS path; aiohttp and urllib3 likewise bind literal loopback/raw sockets.

## Proven root cause
CPython `HTTPServer.server_bind` calls `socket.getfqdn(host)` after binding. On GitHub macOS runners, reverse resolution of numeric `127.0.0.1` repeatedly waits about 35 seconds. The editor workflow constructs `ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), ...)`, so every affected test worker pays a network-environment-dependent lookup even though only loopback bind/address behavior is contractual.

## Plan
- Inventory existing editor-server tests and freeze a held-out behavioral oracle: editor workflow starts a real loopback server even when `socket.getfqdn` raises, and still publishes the literal bound address/port needed by clients.
- Prove the oracle RED against current main for the expected reverse-DNS reason.
- With the oracle held out from the fixer, introduce a local ThreadingHTTPServer subclass whose bind path delegates to `socketserver.TCPServer.server_bind` and derives `server_name`/`server_port` from the already-bound literal address, matching the established pip pattern without adding a dependency.
- Restore the oracle and prove GREEN; defect-seed the original HTTPServer bind path to return it to RED, then restore the fix.
- Run focused editor tests, lint, typecheck, and applicable workflow/action guards.
- Land through Gerrit, then use a full macOS Verify run to confirm the 35-second span disappears while real editor behavior remains covered.

## Caller safety
Expected post-fix behavior: all editor-workflow callers receive the same localhost URL, token, request handling, and shutdown behavior; only an unused reverse-DNS-derived `server_name` value becomes the literal bound host. Before repair, sweep all `ThreadingHTTPServer` and editor workflow callers up to three levels for any dependency on reverse-resolved `server_name`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A behavioral oracle is observed RED first because current server construction invokes `socket.getfqdn`.
- [ ] Editor workflow starts and serves over real loopback without invoking reverse DNS.
- [ ] Bound address/ephemeral port, request handling, authentication, and shutdown coverage remain intact.
- [ ] No new dependency, external call, skip, xfail, or weakened assertion is introduced.
- [ ] The defect-seeded original bind path makes the held-out oracle RED again.
- [ ] Focused tests, lint, typecheck, and applicable CI policy gates pass.
- [ ] Gerrit LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1 precede merge.
- [ ] A post-fix macOS Verify observation records the removed span and wall-clock effect.
data.title: Avoid reverse DNS in loopback editor test server
